exam_name: ISTQB Certified Tester Test Automation Strategy

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: Which of the following is a typical benefit of test automation?

options.A: All manual testing can be removed from the project without any loss of coverage
options.B: The released software is guaranteed to contain no remaining defects
options.C: Repetitive tests, such as regression suites, can be executed faster and more often
options.D: The need for test design and test analysis is removed once tools are in place

questions.explanation: Automation speeds up and repeats execution of stable tests. It does not remove the need for test design, cannot guarantee defect-free software and does not replace every kind of manual testing.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: Which of the following is a typical risk of a test automation initiative?

options.A: Unrealistic expectations about what the tools and the automation effort can deliver
options.B: Automated tests cannot be stored in the same repository as the product code
options.C: Automated tests always take longer to run than the same tests executed manually
options.D: Automation makes it impossible to run tests outside normal working hours

questions.explanation: Overestimating benefits or underestimating effort is a well-known risk. The other statements are false: automated tests usually run faster, can run unattended and can be version controlled.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: Automated regression tests are mainly effective at doing which of the following?

options.A: Discovering new kinds of defects that nobody had thought to look for
options.B: Detecting unintended side effects of changes in functionality that worked before
options.C: Replacing exploratory testing sessions carried out by experienced testers
options.D: Judging whether a new screen layout feels intuitive to real users

questions.explanation: Regression tests re-run known checks to reveal side effects of changes. Finding unforeseen defects and judging usability are better served by exploratory and human-centered testing.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: In the test automation pyramid, which level normally contains the largest number of automated tests?

options.A: Manual acceptance tests carried out by business users
options.B: Unit (component) tests
options.C: End-to-end tests driven through the user interface
options.D: Exploratory tests documented as charters

questions.explanation: The pyramid recommends many fast, cheap unit tests at the base, fewer integration tests in the middle and only a few slow, brittle UI end-to-end tests at the top.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: Which characteristic of the system under test (SUT) most supports test automation?

options.A: A large number of undocumented features that are only known to the original developers
options.B: Business logic that is tightly coupled to the user interface layer of the application
options.C: Frequent changes to interfaces that are not announced to the test team in advance
options.D: Testability features such as stable interfaces and hooks for controlling and observing behavior

questions.explanation: Stable, well-defined interfaces and the ability to control and observe the SUT make automated tests easier to build and maintain. The other characteristics increase automation effort.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: Which of the following is usually a poor candidate for automation?

options.A: Judging whether a redesigned screen feels intuitive and pleasant to real users
options.B: A smoke test that has to be run after each deployment to an environment
options.C: A stable regression check that has to be executed for every build
options.D: A data-driven check that has to be repeated with hundreds of input combinations

questions.explanation: Judgments that depend on human perception, such as usability and look and feel, are difficult to automate. Stable, repetitive and data-heavy checks are typically good candidates.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: Why is the return on investment (ROI) of test automation usually not immediate?

options.A: Automated tests are only allowed to run once a specific number of releases has been made
options.B: The effort to build the solution is recovered only through repeated executions over time
options.C: Automated tests produce no results until the manual tests for the same area have been retired
options.D: Tool vendors delay the delivery of licenses until the organization has finished its pilot

questions.explanation: Automation needs up-front investment in tools, design and scripts. Savings appear as the automated tests are executed many times, so payback takes time.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: What does an automated test need in order to decide automatically whether it has passed or failed?

options.A: A log file containing every message that the system under test has ever produced
options.B: A second copy of the system under test that is always kept in an identical state
options.C: A separate manual tester who reviews every result and confirms the outcome by hand
options.D: A test oracle that provides the expected results to compare with the actual results

questions.explanation: An oracle supplies expected results, for example from a specification or a reference implementation, so that the automation can compare them with actual behavior and report a verdict.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: How does a test automation strategy relate to the organization's overall test strategy?

options.A: It is only a list of the tools that have been licensed by the organization for testing
options.B: It is independent of the overall test strategy and may contradict it where tools require this
options.C: It replaces the overall test strategy once the first automated tests have been created
options.D: It refines the overall test strategy for the automation aspects and must stay consistent with it

questions.explanation: An automation strategy specializes the test strategy for automation, covering objectives, scope, approach and resources, and it should support the overall goals rather than compete with them.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: Which of the following is a key criterion when selecting a test automation tool?

options.A: Its compatibility with the technologies used by the system under test
options.B: The tool's ability to run only on the tester's personal computer
options.C: The number of features in the tool that will not be used in the project
options.D: The popularity of the tool's logo among members of the development team

questions.explanation: A tool must work with the SUT's technologies, for example its UI framework and protocols. Popularity, unused features and single-machine operation are not sound selection criteria.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: Which statement about open-source automation tools is typically true?

options.A: They usually have no license fee, but the organization must provide its own support and expertise
options.B: They always cost more than commercial tools because every feature has to be paid for separately
options.C: They come with a guaranteed response time from a vendor for every defect that is found
options.D: They cannot be used in commercial projects under any circumstances

questions.explanation: Open-source tools avoid license fees but shift responsibility for support, maintenance and skills to the user. Other statements are not generally true.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: What is a risk of choosing a proprietary tool with a specific vendor?

options.A: The vendor is allowed to read every test that is written with the tool at any time
options.B: The tool will stop working on the first day of the month after the pilot
options.C: Dependence on the vendor for licenses, updates and the future direction of the tool
options.D: The tool can never be used together with any other tool in the same project

questions.explanation: Vendor lock-in means that pricing, product roadmap and support depend on one supplier, which the organization should consider in its selection.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: Which factor should mainly drive the choice of the scripting language for automation code?

options.A: The language with the shortest name, since shorter names lead to faster scripts
options.B: The language that was most recently announced at an industry conference
options.C: The language that the vendor of the operating system recommends for office documents
options.D: The skills that are available in the team and the compatibility with the tool and the SUT

questions.explanation: Using a language the team already knows and that the tool and the SUT support reduces training effort and speeds up development and maintenance.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: A team needs to run automated tests on many models of mobile phones. Which resource helps most?

options.A: A device farm, on premises or in the cloud, that gives access to many real or virtual devices
options.B: A larger monitor for each tester, so that more of the screen can be seen at once
options.C: A faster network switch in the office, which makes the phones run apps more quickly
options.D: A single flagship phone that is passed around among all of the testers in the team

questions.explanation: Device farms provide access to a range of devices and operating system versions without buying and maintaining them all, which supports broader coverage.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: Which license type allows a limited pool of licenses to be shared by many users, each using a license only while working?

options.A: A perpetual license that is valid only for one named person
options.B: A trial license that expires after a fixed number of days
options.C: A node-locked license that is tied to one specific computer
options.D: A floating (concurrent-user) license

questions.explanation: Floating licenses are checked out from a pool when needed, which suits teams whose members do not all use the tool at the same time.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: When could building a custom in-house automation tool be a reasonable decision?

options.A: When no available tool meets the specific needs and the organization can maintain the custom tool
options.B: When the organization has no programmers and does not plan to hire any
options.C: When the team wants to avoid the effort of writing any requirements for the tool
options.D: When commercial tools are known to be free of any defects and are cheap to purchase

questions.explanation: Building a tool can be justified if no existing option fits and there is capacity to maintain it. Otherwise, buying or adopting an existing tool is usually cheaper and less risky.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: What is a main benefit of integrating the automation with a test management tool?

options.A: The automated tests no longer need a system under test in order to be executed
options.B: The test management tool will write the automated test scripts without human input
options.C: Automated results can be linked to test cases and requirements for traceability and reporting
options.D: The number of defects in the system under test is reduced automatically

questions.explanation: Integration lets results flow into the test management tool, connecting them with test cases, requirements and reports for a consistent view of testing progress.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: What does service virtualization provide for test automation?

options.A: A method of converting a physical server into a running virtual machine image
options.B: A guarantee that the real services will never change their interfaces
options.C: Simulated versions of unavailable or costly dependencies so that tests can run reliably
options.D: A tool that writes the automated test scripts for the services under test

questions.explanation: Service virtualization simulates the behavior of dependencies, such as third-party services, so automated tests do not depend on their availability, cost or test data.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: Why should an environment health check be run before an automated suite starts?

options.A: To avoid reporting failures that are caused by an unavailable or misconfigured environment
options.B: To make sure that the test scripts are written in the correct language
options.C: To increase the number of defects that the automated tests are able to find
options.D: To remove the need for logging in the automated tests that follow

questions.explanation: A quick check of the environment prevents wasted runs and misleading failures, so that failures can be attributed to the SUT or the tests rather than to the environment.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: What does configuration drift in a test environment mean?

options.A: The environment moves from one data center to another data center automatically
options.B: The environment gradually differs from its intended or documented configuration
options.C: The network speed of the environment becomes faster over the course of the project
options.D: The test cases drift from the requirements that they were written to cover

questions.explanation: Unmanaged manual changes cause the environment to diverge from its baseline, which can make test results unreliable and hard to reproduce.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: Production data is copied into a test environment. Which measure best protects privacy?

options.A: Masking or anonymizing personal data before it is used for testing
options.B: Renaming the test environment so that it does not contain the word production
options.C: Keeping the copy unchanged because test environments are never attacked
options.D: Giving every tester full access so that any misuse can be noticed quickly

questions.explanation: Masking or anonymization removes or obscures personal information while keeping the data useful for tests, which supports compliance with privacy rules.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: Several teams share one test environment and their automated runs interfere with each other. Which measure best reduces the conflicts?

options.A: Asking every team to run its tests at the same moment to finish faster
options.B: Removing the logging so that the runs no longer write to the same place
options.C: Letting each team change the configuration whenever it needs to
options.D: Scheduling or reserving the environment for defined time slots per team

questions.explanation: Reservations and schedules coordinate access to a shared resource, avoiding overlapping runs and unexpected changes in the middle of a test.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: How does a cross-browser test grid help test automation?

options.A: It writes different tests for each browser without any input from the test team
options.B: It runs the same tests against many browser and platform combinations, often in parallel
options.C: It removes the need for the application to be compatible with any browser
options.D: It stores the test results in a format that cannot be read by other tools

questions.explanation: A grid distributes test execution across many browser and operating system combinations, increasing compatibility coverage and reducing total execution time.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: What is a benefit of storing the environment configuration in version control?

options.A: The configuration changes cannot be seen by anyone other than the author
options.B: The environment no longer needs any hardware or cloud resources
options.C: Environment setups can be reproduced and compared over time
options.D: The tests run faster because the configuration is read from a repository

questions.explanation: Versioned configuration documents how an environment was built, allows recreating it and makes changes visible and reviewable.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: Where do automated tests typically run in a continuous integration setup?

options.A: On build agents or runners that are provisioned by the CI server
options.B: On the printer server that is located on the same network as the CI server
options.C: Only inside the production environment used by real customers
options.D: On the personal laptop of the developer who wrote the most recent change

questions.explanation: CI servers schedule jobs on agents or runners that provide the needed tools and environment, so that tests execute consistently for every change.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Which of the following is a typical objective of a test automation pilot project?

options.A: Proving that manual testing is no longer needed in any part of the organization
options.B: Automating every existing test case in the organization within the pilot period
options.C: Gaining experience with the tool and approach and checking that benefits are achievable
options.D: Selecting the tool that has the lowest price without evaluating any technical fit

questions.explanation: Pilots test the solution on a limited scope to learn, refine standards and confirm feasibility and benefits before a wider rollout.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Which activity typically follows a successful pilot?

options.A: Discarding the tool and all pilot results so that the next project starts from scratch
options.B: Freezing the solution so that no further changes to the approach are allowed
options.C: Automating all remaining test cases at once for every project in a single release
options.D: Incremental deployment to further projects, using the lessons learned in the pilot

questions.explanation: After a pilot, the approach is usually rolled out gradually, applying what was learned about tooling, standards, effort and support needs.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: What does continuous integration do with automated tests?

options.A: It replaces them with manual tests that are run once at the end of the release
options.B: It runs them automatically whenever code changes are integrated, giving fast feedback
options.C: It only runs the tests when a manager approves each individual run
options.D: It deletes the tests that pass so that only failing tests remain in the suite

questions.explanation: In continuous integration each integration triggers a build and automated tests, so that problems introduced by a change are found quickly.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: What is the purpose of an automated quality gate in a delivery pipeline?

options.A: To notify customers about the defects that were found in a build
options.B: To rename the build so that it matches the release naming convention
options.C: To stop the promotion of a build when defined test criteria are not met
options.D: To speed up every build by skipping all of the tests in the pipeline

questions.explanation: A quality gate checks results against defined criteria, such as test pass rate, and blocks progress to the next stage if they are not satisfied.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Why are fast automated tests usually placed early in a delivery pipeline?

options.A: Because early stages have more computing power available than later stages
options.B: Because fast tests always find more defects than slow tests do
options.C: Because slow tests are not allowed to be part of a delivery pipeline
options.D: To give developers quick feedback before slower and more expensive tests are run

questions.explanation: Ordering tests from fast to slow shortens the time to first feedback and avoids spending time on long-running tests for builds that already fail basic checks.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: What is a canary release?

options.A: A release that exposes a new version to a small subset of users before wider rollout
options.B: A release that is deployed to all users at the same moment as a precaution
options.C: A release that contains only documentation changes and no code changes
options.D: A release that is only tested by the developers who wrote the code

questions.explanation: Canary releases limit risk by observing a new version with a small share of real traffic before extending it to everyone.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: How should automated test results be used in a release decision?

options.A: As the only input, because manual findings are not reliable for release decisions
options.B: Combined with other information such as risk, open defects and manual findings
options.C: Used only when all of the tests have passed, and otherwise discarded
options.D: Ignored, because release decisions are made only on the basis of the calendar

questions.explanation: Automated results are valuable evidence but should be considered together with risk, defect status and other test findings when deciding on a release.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Which activity best supports the adoption of a shared automation solution across many teams?

options.A: Removing all documentation to avoid confusion between different versions
options.B: Providing training, documentation and support channels to the teams
options.C: Prohibiting teams from asking questions until they have used the tool for a year
options.D: Sending an email with the tool's installation folder and no further guidance

questions.explanation: Adoption depends on enabling people, so training, clear documentation and accessible support help teams use the solution effectively.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: Which responsibility best fits the test automation manager role?

options.A: Writing all of the automated test scripts personally for every project
options.B: Operating the production servers on which real customers are served
options.C: Planning and managing the automation effort, and reporting to stakeholders
options.D: Approving each defect report before it is entered in the defect tracker

questions.explanation: The manager plans and controls the automation work, manages resources, budget and risks, and communicates results and progress to stakeholders.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: Designing the automation architecture and selecting its main components is typically a task of which role?

options.A: The operations engineer who monitors the production environment
options.B: The test automation architect
options.C: The technical writer who prepares the user manuals for the product
options.D: The end user who tests the system in the acceptance phase

questions.explanation: The architect defines the structure of the automation solution and its components, including framework and tool choices, so that it is maintainable and fits the SUT.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: Which role typically implements and maintains automated test scripts?

options.A: The chief executive officer of the organization
options.B: The test automation engineer
options.C: The procurement specialist who negotiates the tool licenses
options.D: The sales representative of the tool vendor

questions.explanation: Test automation engineers develop, execute and maintain the automated tests and supporting code in line with the architecture.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: Which combination of skills is most useful for a test automation engineer?

options.A: Network cabling skills together with experience in facility management
options.B: Testing knowledge together with programming and tool skills
options.C: Legal knowledge together with experience in recruiting new staff
options.D: Graphic design skills together with knowledge of accounting rules

questions.explanation: Automation engineers need to know what to test and how, and also how to build robust code with the tools and languages in use.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: In a centralized automation team model, where is the automation expertise located?

options.A: Spread out with each developer working alone on their own scripts
options.B: Concentrated in one team that serves several projects
options.C: Held by the end users, who write the tests for their own use
options.D: Owned only by external vendors, with none inside the organization

questions.explanation: A centralized team holds specialists together and supports multiple projects, which helps consistency but can create a bottleneck if demand is high.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: What is the main purpose of a community of practice for test automation?

options.A: Limiting the number of people allowed to talk about automation in the company
options.B: Providing a legal entity that owns all of the automation code of the company
options.C: Replacing all managers with a group of volunteers who vote on every decision
options.D: Sharing knowledge and good practices across teams without changing reporting lines

questions.explanation: Communities of practice connect people with a shared interest so they exchange experience, solve problems and improve practices, even if they belong to different teams.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: Relying on one person who is the only one who understands the automation framework creates which risk?

options.A: Loss of knowledge and delivery capability if the person leaves or is unavailable
options.B: A guarantee that no defects can be introduced into the framework
options.C: An unlimited increase in the execution speed of every automated test
options.D: Automatic documentation of the framework by the system itself

questions.explanation: Single points of knowledge threaten continuity, so knowledge should be shared through documentation, reviews and pairing.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: What should be planned when automation development is outsourced to another company?

options.A: A contract that forbids the organization from ever looking at the delivered code
options.B: A plan to stop maintaining the automation once the outsourcing contract ends
options.C: Knowledge transfer and access to the code so the organization can maintain the automation
options.D: A requirement that the supplier never communicates with the internal test team

questions.explanation: Without knowledge transfer and access, the organization risks dependency on the supplier and cannot maintain or evolve the automation itself.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: Why are communication skills important for people working on test automation?

options.A: Because the tools refuse to run unless the user has completed a language course
options.B: Because good communicators do not need to learn any tools or programming languages
options.C: Because automated tests can only be executed if the tester speaks during the run
options.D: They must coordinate with developers, testers and managers about changes and results

questions.explanation: Automation work depends on cooperation across roles, for example agreeing on testability, explaining results and aligning priorities.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an external metric of test automation benefit?

options.A: The number of classes defined in the test library
options.B: The reduction in manual regression testing effort
options.C: The average number of statements in each automated script
options.D: The number of lines of code in the automation framework

questions.explanation: External metrics describe the benefits of automation for the project or organization, such as saved effort. Code size and structure measures describe the solution itself.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an internal metric of the test automation solution?

options.A: The revenue of the product tested by the automated tests
options.B: The number of customers who use the released software
options.C: The number of production incidents in the previous year
options.D: The effort spent each month on maintaining the automated scripts

questions.explanation: Internal metrics describe the solution, such as maintenance effort, script failures caused by automation defects and script size, helping to manage its quality and cost.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: What characterizes data-driven test automation?

options.A: Test data is separated from the script logic and read from an external source
options.B: Every test contains its own hard-coded values that cannot be changed
options.C: Tests are written as natural-language sentences that are never executed
options.D: The data of the system under test is deleted after every automated run

questions.explanation: In a data-driven approach the same script is run with different data sets from files or tables, which increases coverage with little extra script code.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: In keyword-driven test automation, how are the test steps typically expressed?

options.A: Test steps are expressed with keywords that map to implemented actions
options.B: Test data is generated at random without any documented expected results
options.C: Test cases are recorded once and can never be edited afterwards
options.D: Test scripts can only be run by the developer who wrote the keywords

questions.explanation: Keyword-driven tests use readable keywords for actions, implemented once in the framework, so that testers can compose tests without detailed programming.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: An automated test fails. What is the first useful step in the analysis?

options.A: Delete the test so that the failure no longer appears in the results
options.B: Rerun the test until it passes and then ignore the earlier failures
options.C: Find out whether the cause is a SUT defect, a script problem or an environment issue
options.D: Report a defect in the SUT immediately without looking at the failure details

questions.explanation: Failures can stem from the SUT, the automation or the environment. Classifying the cause first ensures the right people fix the right thing.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Why should automation code be stored in version control?

options.A: To avoid having to write any documentation for the automation solution
options.B: To prevent anyone other than the original author from reading the code
options.C: To track changes, enable collaboration and allow a return to earlier versions
options.D: To make the code run faster during the automated test execution

questions.explanation: Version control records history, supports parallel work and makes it possible to compare and restore earlier versions of the code, as with production code.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: What do coding standards for automation code mainly support?

options.A: Longer execution times that give tests more time to detect defects
options.B: Readability and maintainability across the team
options.C: A larger number of scripts for the same amount of tested functionality
options.D: The removal of any need for reviews of the automation code

questions.explanation: Consistent naming, structure and style make code easier to read, review and change, which lowers maintenance effort.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: How does good logging in automated tests help the team?

options.A: It allows failures to be analyzed without rerunning the test
options.B: It replaces the need for expected results in every test
options.C: It guarantees that automated tests will never fail
options.D: It reduces the number of environments needed to run the tests

questions.explanation: Detailed, well-structured logs record what happened during execution, so the cause of a failure can be found quickly, even for failures that are hard to reproduce.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: Why should the objectives of a test automation initiative be measurable?

options.A: So that progress can be checked and it can be shown whether the objectives have been achieved
options.B: So that the objectives never need to be discussed with the stakeholders again
options.C: So that the objectives can be met by simply reporting that the work was done
options.D: So that the objectives can be changed each week without anyone noticing the changes

questions.explanation: Measurable objectives, such as a target reduction in regression effort, make it possible to track results and to judge success objectively.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: A team automates poorly designed test cases. What is the most likely outcome?

options.A: The poorly designed tests become good tests because they are now executed by a computer
options.B: The automation tool improves the test cases while running them so that quality rises
options.C: The automated tests execute the same weaknesses faster and more often, without improving test quality
options.D: The system under test becomes more reliable because it is exercised more frequently

questions.explanation: Automation does not fix weak test design. Poor tests remain poor, and automating them only repeats their weaknesses with more speed.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: Why does the effort to maintain automated tests tend to grow over time?

options.A: Automated tests are only valid for a period of one month after they are written
options.B: Automated tests slowly forget the steps they were written to execute
options.C: Changes in the system under test require the automated tests to be adapted
options.D: Tools deliberately increase the size of scripts to justify more licenses

questions.explanation: As the SUT evolves, interfaces, data and behavior change, so scripts must be updated. Maintainable design keeps this effort under control.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: Which statement about test automation is correct?

options.A: Automation solutions are software projects needing design, coding and testing
options.B: Automation code does not need to be tested because tools are always correct
options.C: Automation is a one-time activity that is finished when the first scripts run
options.D: Automation can be done well without any knowledge of programming or design

questions.explanation: Automation solutions are software and require the same engineering discipline as other software: architecture, coding standards, testing and maintenance.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: At which test levels can test automation be applied?

options.A: Only at the acceptance level, because the other levels cannot be automated
options.B: Only at the component level, because higher levels have no repeatable steps
options.C: At several levels, including component, integration, system and acceptance testing
options.D: Only during production operation, after the software has been released

questions.explanation: Automation can support all test levels, and the best mix depends on cost, speed and risk, for example many unit tests and fewer end-to-end tests.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: Why is automation especially valuable for load and performance testing?

options.A: Because load tests do not need any environment or test data
options.B: Because performance requirements never change during the project
options.C: Simulating many simultaneous users is not practical manually
options.D: Because manual testers are not allowed to observe response times

questions.explanation: Simulating thousands of concurrent users and measuring response times needs tools, so such testing is difficult to carry out without automation.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: How does automation contribute to consistency of test execution?

options.A: It changes the steps slightly on each run to explore different behavior
options.B: It executes the same steps in the same way every time, which reduces human error
options.C: It skips steps that are considered unimportant by the tool
options.D: It relies on the tester to remember the steps between the different runs

questions.explanation: Automated tests repeat the defined steps exactly, avoiding slips and variation that occur when people execute repetitive tests manually.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: How should the tests to be automated first be prioritized?

options.A: By choosing the tests that are the most difficult to automate to learn the tool quickly
options.B: By alphabetical order of the test case names in the test management tool
options.C: By risk and expected value, for example stable, frequently executed and business-critical tests first
options.D: By choosing tests at random so that no area is favored over any other area

questions.explanation: Prioritizing by risk, frequency and stability gives the earliest and largest return and avoids investing in tests that change often or bring little value.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: What should an effort estimate for an automation task include?

options.A: Design, implementation, review and the expected ongoing maintenance
options.B: Only the time that the tool needs to execute the script once
options.C: Only the license cost of the tool, without any staff effort
options.D: Only the time needed to press the record button in the tool

questions.explanation: Automation effort covers creating, reviewing and stabilizing the scripts, and maintaining them later. Estimating only recording or execution time underestimates the work.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: What is a test data generation tool used for?

options.A: Deleting the defects that were found in the system under test
options.B: Writing the requirements for the next release of the software
options.C: Measuring how many users are logged in to the production system
options.D: Creating data sets that can be used as input for tests

questions.explanation: Data generators produce synthetic or derived data with the needed characteristics, which supports testing when real data is unavailable, sensitive or insufficient.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: What is the purpose of a static analysis tool applied to automation code?

options.A: To replace the code reviews performed by the members of the team
options.B: To execute the tests of the code in a production-like environment
options.C: To find rule violations and other code issues without running the code
options.D: To translate the code into a different programming language

questions.explanation: Static analysis inspects source code for issues such as style violations, potential defects and complexity, helping keep automation code maintainable.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: What does a continuous integration server provide as a resource for test automation?

options.A: A tool that designs the user interface of the system under test
options.B: A place where the requirements for the system are negotiated
options.C: A database in which customer orders of the production system are stored
options.D: Automated execution of builds and tests, triggered by changes or schedules

questions.explanation: A CI server orchestrates builds and test runs, provides logs and results, and makes automated execution a routine part of development.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: Which resource lets an organization pay for test execution capacity only when it is used?

options.A: Perpetual licenses that are bought once for each tester
options.B: Cloud-based test execution services with usage-based pricing
options.C: Servers that are purchased for a period of five years
options.D: Printed test scripts that are stored in a filing cabinet

questions.explanation: Cloud services can supply environments and devices on demand and charge for use, which is helpful for variable or peak demand.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: Why should the learning curve be considered when planning automation resources?

options.A: Because tools become slower as the team learns more about them
options.B: Team members need time to learn the tools and approach before they are fully productive
options.C: Because a longer learning curve always results in a better return on investment
options.D: Because team members must not use a tool before the vendor has trained them

questions.explanation: Initial productivity is lower while people learn, so plans should allow time for training and practice instead of assuming full output from day one.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: Which factor is useful when judging the long-term viability of a tool?

options.A: The vendor's support and the size and activity of the user community
options.B: The tool's version number compared with those of other tools
options.C: The color scheme used in the tool's user interface
options.D: The number of pages in the license agreement of the tool

questions.explanation: Good support and an active community suggest that problems will be resolved and that the tool will continue to be maintained and improved.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: What is the benefit of a well-designed keyword library that many projects can share?

options.A: Each project must rewrite every keyword before it can use the library
options.B: Reuse of implemented actions lowers the effort to create and maintain tests
options.C: The keywords cannot be changed without asking every project for permission
options.D: The library removes the need for any test design in the projects

questions.explanation: Shared keywords are implemented and maintained once and reused, reducing duplication and effort across projects.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: Why should reporting tools or dashboards be considered a resource for an automation initiative?

options.A: They execute the automated tests instead of the test automation tool
options.B: They remove all failures from the results before those are published
options.C: They prevent stakeholders from asking questions about the results
options.D: They make results and trends visible to stakeholders in an understandable form

questions.explanation: Dashboards turn raw results into information such as pass rates and trends, which supports decisions and stakeholder communication.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: Why should a test environment for automation resemble production?

options.A: So that it costs exactly the same as the production environment
options.B: So that the automated tests no longer need any test data
options.C: Results are more reliable and configuration-related defects are found
options.D: So that the environment can be used by real customers when needed

questions.explanation: A production-like environment reduces the risk that tests pass in test and fail in production because of differences in configuration or infrastructure.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: What does refreshing test data to a baseline before a run achieve?

options.A: It deletes the test scripts that were used in the previous run
options.B: It removes the need to check any results at the end of the run
options.C: It increases the number of users in the production system
options.D: It gives each run a known, repeatable starting state

questions.explanation: Restoring data to a known state makes results reproducible and avoids failures caused by leftovers from earlier runs.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: Why should resource usage of a test environment be monitored during automated runs?

options.A: To replace the logs that are written by the system under test
options.B: To detect capacity problems such as CPU or memory shortages
options.C: To prove that the environment is not being used by anyone
options.D: To reduce the number of tests in the suite whenever usage is high

questions.explanation: Monitoring reveals bottlenecks and instabilities in the environment, which helps explain failures and plan capacity.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: Why is access to a test environment usually controlled?

options.A: To protect data and configuration from unauthorized or accidental changes
options.B: To keep the testers from finding out what the environment contains
options.C: To make the environment slower so that the tests are more thorough
options.D: To ensure that no one is able to run automated tests without a manager

questions.explanation: Controlled access prevents unwanted changes that would make results unreliable and safeguards test data, which may be sensitive.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: Why might a test environment use a sandbox version of a third-party service instead of the real one?

options.A: To make the system under test run in production more quickly
options.B: To avoid testing the integration with the third party at all
options.C: To make sure that the third party can see all of the test data
options.D: To test the integration without real transactions, cost or side effects

questions.explanation: Sandboxes imitate the provider's interface in a safe way, so the integration can be tested without charges, real orders or risk to real data.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: What is the purpose of emulators and simulators in test automation?

options.A: To replace the system under test with a system that always passes
options.B: To imitate devices or hardware so tests can run without the real equipment
options.C: To store the test results in a format that can be read only by the tool
options.D: To prevent tests from running at the same time as other tests

questions.explanation: Emulators and simulators reproduce the behavior of devices or components, which saves cost and makes tests easier to repeat, although real devices remain important for some checks.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: How does automated provisioning of environments benefit test automation?

options.A: Environments can only be created by the person who owns the tool
options.B: Environments are made permanent so that they are never removed
options.C: Environments no longer need any configuration to be run by the tests
options.D: Environments can be created quickly and consistently when they are needed

questions.explanation: Automation of provisioning shortens waiting time and gives the same setup each time, which supports reliable and repeatable test runs.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: Why should someone be made responsible for the environments used by automated tests?

options.A: Because responsibility for an environment is not allowed to be shared
options.B: Because the responsible person must run all of the tests personally
options.C: An owner keeps environments available, configured correctly and maintained
options.D: Because environments do not need any attention when nobody is responsible

questions.explanation: Environments do not maintain themselves, so an owner ensures configuration, availability and change coordination, which reduces test failures due to environment problems.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: How can the regression tests for a release be selected sensibly?

options.A: By running only those tests that have never failed in any earlier release
options.B: By running only the tests whose names start with the letter R
options.C: By running only the tests that were written most recently by the team
options.D: Based on risk and the changes made, so that impacted and critical areas are covered

questions.explanation: Selecting by risk and impact focuses effort on areas most likely to be affected by the change and most important to the business.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: What does continuous deployment add compared with continuous integration?

options.A: Changes that pass the automated checks are released to production automatically
options.B: Changes are integrated by hand at the end of a project
options.C: Changes are never tested before they are released to any environment
options.D: Changes are only made once per year after a long manual approval process

questions.explanation: Continuous deployment extends the pipeline so that every change that passes the defined tests is deployed automatically, which depends on trustworthy automated tests.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: A regression suite takes ten hours and delays the pipeline. Which is a sensible response?

options.A: Delete the tests until the suite is short enough to run in one minute
options.B: Split the suite into stages or parallel jobs and run the most critical tests first
options.C: Run the suite only on the day before the release date
options.D: Run the suite manually so that no pipeline is involved

questions.explanation: Structuring and parallelizing execution shortens feedback time while keeping important coverage. Randomly deleting tests loses coverage.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Why might automated test results have to be retained for a defined period?

options.A: To make the storage system of the organization fill up more quickly
options.B: To prevent the tests from being run again in the future
options.C: To provide evidence for audits and to analyze trends over time
options.D: To make sure the results cannot be viewed by the development team

questions.explanation: Retained results document what was tested and its outcome, which can be needed for compliance and for analysis of quality trends.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: What is a sensible basis for deciding the order in which teams adopt a new automation solution?

options.A: The order in which the teams submitted their holiday requests
options.B: The readiness of the teams and the value expected for each one
options.C: The alphabetical order of the team names in the organization chart
options.D: The teams that are least willing to change should always start first

questions.explanation: Teams that are ready and expected to benefit most are good early adopters, and their success helps other teams to follow.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Which measure indicates the adoption of a shared automation framework across the organization?

options.A: The number of pages of documentation written about the framework
options.B: The number of meetings held about the framework each week
options.C: The number of tools evaluated before the framework was chosen
options.D: The number of teams that actively use the framework in their pipelines

questions.explanation: Actual usage by teams shows whether the framework has been accepted, whereas documentation and meeting counts describe activity rather than adoption.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Why should the timing of an automation rollout be coordinated with other major initiatives?

options.A: Because rollout schedules must always match the dates of public holidays
options.B: Because automation cannot be rolled out while any other initiative exists
options.C: Because other initiatives are always automation projects with the same tools
options.D: Competing initiatives can limit the availability of people, environments and attention

questions.explanation: Rollouts need people, environments and management support, so conflicts with other large initiatives can delay or weaken adoption.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: What is a useful practice when introducing automation to a team that is used to manual testing?

options.A: Replace all manual tests overnight and remove the manual testing role
options.B: Keep the automation hidden from the team until it is finished
options.C: Provide the tool without training and ask the team to work it out
options.D: Start with a limited scope and provide support to build confidence

questions.explanation: A gradual start with support reduces resistance and risk, and lets the team learn from early experience before the scope grows.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Why is it useful to include known limitations of the automation in release information?

options.A: The development team no longer needs to read any test results
options.B: Stakeholders learn to trust that automation has covered every part of the system
options.C: Stakeholders understand which areas are covered by automated checks and which are not
options.D: The limitations remove the need for any manual test after the release

questions.explanation: Transparency about coverage helps stakeholders judge remaining risk and decide where additional testing or caution is needed.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: How does a test analyst contribute to test automation?

options.A: By approving the purchase of the automation tool licenses
options.B: By designing test cases suited to automation and defining expected results
options.C: By operating the network devices on which the automated tests are run
options.D: By deciding which programming language the developers should use

questions.explanation: Analysts bring test design knowledge, identifying valuable tests and expected results, which engineers then implement as automated tests.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: Why should developers be involved in test automation?

options.A: They can write unit tests and help make the system testable
options.B: They are responsible for the tool licenses of the organization
options.C: They must replace all testers so that no testers are needed
options.D: They are the only people who are allowed to run automated tests

questions.explanation: Developers contribute at the lower levels, such as unit tests, and can design interfaces and hooks that make higher-level automation easier.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: Which approach supports the development of automation skills in a team?

options.A: Prohibiting people from experimenting with the tools during working hours
options.B: Handing out a single manual and expecting immediate expertise
options.C: A mix of workshops, mentoring and practice on real tasks
options.D: Allowing only external consultants to work with the tools

questions.explanation: Skills grow through learning combined with guided practice, for example mentoring and applying new techniques to real automation tasks.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: When building an automation team, which composition is often effective?

options.A: Only managers, because they know how to make decisions
options.B: Only people who have never written or run a test before
options.C: People with testing knowledge and people with programming skills
options.D: Only people who work exclusively on the production systems

questions.explanation: Automation needs both test design insight and engineering skills, so a mix of backgrounds covers what to test and how to implement it.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: Why is shared ownership of the automation code valuable?

options.A: Only managers can approve changes to the code
options.B: Several people can maintain the code, reducing dependence on individuals
options.C: Nobody is responsible for the quality of the code anymore
options.D: The code is not allowed to be changed after it has been written

questions.explanation: When more than one person knows and can maintain the code, work continues despite absences and the quality benefits from different views.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: How can recognizing contributions help an automation initiative?

options.A: It motivates people and encourages continued effort and sharing of good practices
options.B: It ensures that nobody else will want to contribute to the initiative
options.C: It removes the need for any objectives to be defined for the initiative
options.D: It replaces the salary of the people who work on the initiative

questions.explanation: Recognition supports engagement and retention, and it encourages others to contribute and share what they learn.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: What is a challenge for distributed automation teams that work in different time zones?

options.A: All team members must work exactly the same hours to be effective
options.B: Running tests in different places is not possible with any tool
options.C: Coordinating communication and handovers so that work is not blocked
options.D: The same source code cannot be shared by people in different locations

questions.explanation: Distribution makes real-time communication harder, so clear documentation, shared tools and defined handovers help keep work flowing.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: What is the role of a product owner or business stakeholder in test automation?

options.A: Helping to set priorities for automation based on business value and risk
options.B: Choosing the file names for all automated test scripts
options.C: Operating the build servers that run the automated tests
options.D: Writing the automation code in place of the automation engineers

questions.explanation: Business stakeholders know which functions matter most, so their input guides what is worth automating and reviewing results in business terms.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Why should the automated test suite be reviewed regularly for duplicated tests?

options.A: Duplicates improve accuracy because the same test is checked twice
options.B: Duplicates are required by the tools in order to report results
options.C: Duplicates add execution time and maintenance effort without adding coverage
options.D: Duplicates make the suite run faster because there are more tests

questions.explanation: Overlapping tests cost time and effort in execution and maintenance, so removing or consolidating them keeps the suite efficient.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: How does an abstraction layer, such as page objects, reduce maintenance effort?

options.A: It removes the need to understand the application under test
options.B: It stops the user interface from ever changing during the project
options.C: It makes every test run in exactly the same time
options.D: Interface changes are fixed in one place rather than in every test

questions.explanation: Separating tests from interface details localizes the impact of change, so many tests can keep working after a single fix.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: How often should automation results be reported to stakeholders?

options.A: At regular, agreed intervals with audience-suited detail
options.B: Never, because stakeholders are not interested in results
options.C: Only when there is a failure and never when tests pass
options.D: Only when the project has been completely finished

questions.explanation: Regular reporting keeps stakeholders informed and supports decisions, and the level of detail should match what each audience needs.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: What is a false positive in automated testing?

options.A: A test fails although the system under test behaves correctly
options.B: A test is skipped because the tool was not licensed
options.C: A test runs with data that has been generated at random
options.D: A test passes although the system under test contains a defect

questions.explanation: False positives report problems that are not defects in the SUT, for example caused by script or environment issues. They waste analysis effort and reduce trust in the results.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: What is a false negative in automated testing?

options.A: A test fails although the system under test behaves correctly
options.B: A test is written in a language that the tool does not support
options.C: A test is repeated because the results were not stored
options.D: A test passes although the system under test contains a defect

questions.explanation: False negatives miss real defects, giving unwarranted confidence. They are especially dangerous because nobody investigates a test that passes.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Why are explicit waits preferred over fixed sleeps in automated UI tests?

options.A: They make the test wait for the same amount of time in every case
options.B: They remove the need for any synchronization with the system under test
options.C: They cause the test to skip steps that take a long time to complete
options.D: They wait for a condition to be met, which makes tests more reliable and often faster

questions.explanation: Waiting for a specific condition adapts to actual response times, while fixed sleeps are either too short, causing failures, or too long, wasting time.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: What is the purpose of refactoring automation code?

options.A: To reduce the number of requirements covered by the tests
options.B: To improve structure and readability without changing test behavior
options.C: To add new features to the system under test
options.D: To hide defects in the code so that they are not reported

questions.explanation: Refactoring cleans up design, removes duplication and improves clarity, keeping the code maintainable as the suite grows.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: What can trend analysis of automated suite execution time reveal?

options.A: The exact number of defects that will be found in the next release
options.B: Whether the automation tool has been licensed correctly
options.C: Which team members are the least productive during the project
options.D: Run time growth that may call for parallelization or test selection

questions.explanation: Watching execution time over releases shows when the suite becomes too slow for its purpose, prompting action to keep feedback fast.
